refused.reason: run run-B changed name-of-h2 after this run began, so undoing this run beneath it could undo on top of its changes; it has changes of its own to undo, so roll it back first (pleiades rollback run-B), or step over it with --despite-run run-B; one of the two carries no run order (its journal predates run ordering, or it ran under a shared device lease, whose holders overlap), so this was decided by the journals' clock times
rb.copy's undo through rb.edit is partial: it does not put back everything the task overwrote
rb.shell changed the device and cannot be undone (an arbitrary command); give the task a rollback: list in its runbook, or leave the change in place

levels.name: undo tasks[3] (task tasks[3]), step 1: stop it
undo tasks[3] (task tasks[3]), step 2: then remove it

left.reason: rb.shell changed the device and cannot be undone (an arbitrary command); give the task a rollback: list in its runbook, or leave the change in place

unknown.reason: rb.shell failed during its action, so it may have changed part of what it meant to; the journal cannot say what, and nothing undoes it

already_undone.reason: an earlier rollback of this run undid it

nothing_to_undo.reason: its rollback: list is empty, which says undoing it means doing nothing
